meta.title: Connect Email to Windsurf: Cascade MCP Server Setup
meta.description: Add a real inbox to Cascade in Windsurf. One entry in mcp_config.json using serverUrl, then authorize with OAuth. No API key. One inbox free.

hero.lead: Add a real mailbox to Cascade in Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf. Read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and organize mail from the editor, across every inbox you have connected.
hero.answer: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf. In the Cascade panel, open the ... menu at the top right and click Open MCP config file in the MCPs section. Add one entry under mcpServers using the field serverUrl, not url, with https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp, save the file, and sign in with MCPEmails when prompted.

method.title: How Windsurf connects: OAuth, no API key
method.body: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) runs the standard MCP OAuth flow against this server. It registers itself with RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, so there is no client ID to create, and authorizes with authorization code plus PKCE using S256. No client secret is ever transmitted, and the token carries only the scopes you approve on our consent screen. The access token it receives lasts an hour and refreshes itself; it is listed in Dashboard, API Keys as OAuth: followed by the client name, which is where you revoke the connection.

setup.h: Create a free account and connect a mailbox
setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com, no card required, then go to Dashboard, Inboxes, Connect Inbox. Outlook and Microsoft 365 connect with Sign in with Microsoft; Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex take an app-specific password; anything else connects over plain IMAP and SMTP. The free plan holds one inbox, forever.

In the Cascade panel, click the ... menu at the top right, and in the MCPs section click Open MCP config file. The file is ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json on macOS and Linux, and %APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json on Windows.
Add the entry below. The field name here is serverUrl, not url.
Save the file and sign in with MCPEmails when prompted. Approve the scopes you want Cascade to hold.

gotchas.h: The field is serverUrl, and url fails silently
gotchas.p: This is the single most common Windsurf setup mistake, and it is entirely reasonable to make: Cursor, Zed and VS Code all read url, so a snippet copied from any of them looks right. Devin Desktop reads serverUrl. With the wrong key the entry parses, the server appears in the list, and no tools ever arrive.

gotchas.h: Older guides point at the Windsurf config path
gotchas.p: Windsurf kept its MCP config in ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json, and many guides still say so. Devin Desktop uses ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json (%APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json on Windows). The Open MCP config file item in the Cascade ... menu opens the file it actually reads, so start there rather than typing a path.

gotchas.h: Decide up front whether Cascade should be able to send
gotchas.p: The consent screen is where that is settled. Read and draft scopes suit an editor assistant, and leaving send:email off means no prompt, no jailbreak and no confused loop can dispatch mail from this connection. Human approval in the dashboard is the belt-and-braces version if you do want sending.

limits: Requests are rate limited per key in per-minute, hourly and daily windows sized to your plan, so one key can use the plan's full per-minute ceiling and several keys share it. A 429 carries Retry-After. Your plan ceiling on billable actions also applies.
The server is request and response only. There are no webhooks and no server-initiated events, so new mail never wakes your agent by itself. To react to arriving mail, poll on a schedule.

Mail is fetched live from your provider on every call and never stored. Only the encrypted OAuth token or app password is kept, so a revoked token or a changed mailbox password ends access immediately.

faq.q: How do I connect email to Windsurf?
faq.a: In Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf, open the ... menu in the Cascade panel and click Open MCP config file. Add an entry under mcpServers with serverUrl set to https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp, save, and sign in with MCPEmails when prompted. Cascade then has tools for reading, searching, sending, replying, forwarding, organizing and scheduling mail.

faq.q: Why does my Windsurf config not work when the same JSON works in Cursor?
faq.a: Almost always the field name. Cursor reads url, Devin Desktop reads serverUrl. The rest of the entry is identical, which is exactly why the mistake survives a careful read.

faq.q: Do I need an API key for Windsurf?
faq.a: No. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) runs the OAuth flow against this server, so the config file holds only a public URL. A bearer API key remains available for scripted or headless use.

faq.q: Which mailboxes can Windsurf reach this way?
faq.a: Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 over Sign in with Microsoft, where a work account may need an IT admin to approve the app once; Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex with an app-specific password; and any other mailbox that speaks IMAP and SMTP on the standard ports. The client sees them all through the same connection: your agent calls inbox_list first to discover every connected mailbox and its id, so there are no UUIDs to paste anywhere.

faq.q: Can Cascade send email without me seeing it?
faq.a: Only if you let it. Sending is gated on the send:email scope, so a key or a token without that scope cannot send at all. On top of that, an inbox owner can require human approval in the dashboard, which holds every send, reply, forward, draft send and scheduled send until a person releases it.

faq.q: Is my email stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Every message is fetched live from your provider for the request that asked for it and handed straight to your client. Only the encrypted OAuth token or app password is kept, so future calls can authenticate. Deleting the inbox in the dashboard, or revoking access at your provider, ends the connection at once.

ctaBand.title: Give Cascade a real inbox
ctaBand.sub: One config entry, one sign-in. One inbox free forever, no card required.
